title: Advanced Electrical Infrastructure Prove Project
summary: Analyze and coordinate a simulated critical-power failure with A/B, capacity, backup, and cross-domain evidence.
objectives: Interpret a synthetic critical-power incident and identify its failure domain and dependencies.
Recommend safe escalation and document validation and recovery criteria.

vocab.def: Unused modeled capacity before a stated scenario limit.
A shared dependency affects apparently separate paths.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This individual proof project is simulation-only. It does not authorize live electrical work, panel access, switchgear operation, UPS service, generator operation, transfer-switch work, or live PDU maintenance.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Scenario inputs include a simplified utility-to-UPS-to-PDU path, A/B state, UPS and generator telemetry, current and projected load, recent maintenance, rack/service impact, network state, and cooling cross-signals. Trace the affected path, compare A/B availability, calculate scenario headroom, identify common dependencies, and distinguish symptoms from causes.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Submit an evidence package with observed conditions, path/failure-domain analysis, units and assumptions, prohibited actions, safe escalation, cross-team handoff, validation, and recovery criteria.

practice.prompt: What should you do when a simulated power incident could involve energized equipment?
practice.answer: Stop physical action, preserve the provided evidence, and escalate to a qualified authorized role.

quiz.question: What is the correct learner action for a modeled switchgear alarm?
options: Interpret the synthetic state and document qualified escalation
